findings.text: Public range release selects an immediate path when running on the selftest task and a deferred path otherwise, after ensuring one time initialization. The immediate path reclaims synchronously while the regular path defers reclamation and waits for readers.

Public per lock reset selects immediate versus deferred reclamation based on whether the caller is the selftest task, after one time initialization. Both paths remove every subclass association for the supplied map.

Public dynamic key removal refuses static objects, unhashes the key under interrupt disabled lock protection, releases classes whose key overlaps the single byte range, decrements the dynamic key count, schedules deferred reclamation when needed, and then waits with an expedited grace period for concurrent key testers.

Early boot reporter logs validator identity, configured sizing limits for subclasses depth keys hashes entries chains, computed memory consumption of core tables plus optional chain and trace tables, and per task held lock storage size. It performs no table initialization in the shown fragment.

Diagnostic entry points expose held lock inspection: one scans the current task held stack for overlap with a freeing range, one reports any remaining held depth, one prints a target task held set unless reporting is disabled, one warns when exiting toward user context with held depth and then clears per call history, and one reports questionable RCU use with scheduler and quiescent state context.

Class teardown first purges every dependency record that mentions the class in either direction and updates the global dependency count. Only when both successor and predecessor sets are empty does it detach the class from hash and list structures, clear identity fields with ordered stores, adjust unused and total class counts and the in use bitmap and high index, and otherwise it emits a one time warning. Chain detachment and a zapped counter update always follow.

Class slot recycling asserts that linkage is present and dependency sets are empty both before and after clearing, and zeroes the object starting at the identity field while preserving list linkage fields that precede it.

Address overlap tests treat ranges as half open intervals. One helper reports containment of an address inside a base plus length window and drives module range teardown by matching either key or name pointers, while the other reports disjointness and drives the held lock freed check by comparing the freeing interval against each held instance.

Deferred reclamation uses two pending slots with a current index and a scheduled flag. Preparation fails when the target slot holds no zapped entries or a callback is already pending, otherwise it marks scheduled and flips the index. The RCU handler reclaims the closed slot, clears scheduled, attempts to arm the other slot, and requeues itself only when arming succeeds. Immediate paths bypass this machine and reclaim synchronously.

Reclamation of a pending slot validates global structures, reinitializes every queued class, moves the whole queue onto the free pool in one splice, and when chain proving is enabled releases chain bitmap entries tracked for that slot and clears the tracking bitmap.

Range teardown walks every hash bucket under RCU protection and zaps classes whose key or name pointer falls inside the supplied window. Per lock reset repeats lookup plus zap for every subclass index and then verifies that no cached class for that map remains registered, disabling further reporting on failure.

Mutating paths disable local interrupts and hold either the main validator lock or the graph lock while selecting a pending slot and zapping, then release in reverse order and restore interrupts. Deferred paths queue an RCU callback outside the critical section. Range release waits for a full grace period before the caller frees module memory, key unregistration waits expedited for key testers, and the RCU handler itself reenters the interrupt disabled locked region to reclaim.

Statistics record accumulates chain lookup hits and misses, hard and soft interrupt transition counts with redundant transition counts, unused lock count, redundant and cyclic search counts, forward and backward usage search counts, and a per key operation counter array indexed by key limit.
Usage encoding reserves value one for read versus write distinction, value two for direction versus state distinction, and defines the remaining bits as state selector by complementing the low two.

Chain context flags use bit zero for soft interrupt context and bit one for hard interrupt context. Total chain capacity is two raised to the chain bits parameter, average depth expectation is five, and total held entry capacity is the product of chain capacity and average depth.

Fallback sizing provides sixteen thousand dependency entries, fifteen chain bits, two hundred sixty two thousand stack entries, and eight thousand stack hash buckets. Configurable sizing instead derives entries and stack capacities as powers of two from dedicated bit count options.
Human readable usage display length is defined as twice the count of usage states plus one for termination.

Usage bits are generated by expanding a shared state list so each abstract state yields four ordered values covering use and enablement each in normal and read form, followed by generic use values and a count sentinel. A parallel flag enumeration maps each usage bit position to a single bit mask, and aggregate masks combine all enabled, all used, and read variants across every state plus combined interrupt groupings.

Statistics read has two builds: one aggregates a named counter across all possible processors by summing per processor instances, the other is a constant zero for builds without statistics. Forward and backward dependency counters in this header are constant zero placeholders.

Proc display iterates the dense class array by numeric position bounded by the current maximum index, with start by offset, advance by one returning null past the end, and empty stop. Each visible entry prints its key identity, optional operation and dependency counts and usage letters when proving is enabled, and its name with optional version and subclass suffixes or a derived key name when unnamed, followed by immediate successors only and a blank separator.

All diagnostic warnings first attempt to disable further reporting and abort when already disabled or when silent mode is set, bracket output with emergency console transitions, and include task identity plus held lock dump and stack trace where relevant. Freed while held, still held at exit, locks held on exit toward user context, and illegal RCU use from offline processors or extended quiescent periods are each treated as one way trip to disabled reporting.

Selftest context is detected by comparing the current task pointer against a dedicated selftest task pointer. Deferred preparation asserts it is never entered in that context, while public range and reset dispatchers use the test to choose synchronous reclamation.
